scenario: AITA for telling my SIL to shut up? | My SIL drives me a little bonkers sometimes. She is extremely proud of things like not watching TV, not listening to pop music, not having Facebook, and she interrupts conversations to say it. Often insulting the thing as well, instead of just saying that she doesn’t like it. Instead it’s about her superiority for not liking it. A few days ago we were having dinner and my 14-year-old sister starts talking about she watched a Marvel movie and she’s looking forward to a sequel that should be coming out soon. My SIL said, “I’ve never watched any Marvel movies. They seem pretty awful.” I was pissed off, I don’t get why my SIL, an adult woman, feels the need to be so rude and dismissive towards a teenager. I said loudly, “shut up, not everything has to be about you and what you like.” She blushed and didn’t say anything more, my brother didn’t say anything either. But he messaged me after they left saying that this was my expression of “always hating” his wife and that I’m a bad person who doesn’t want her to participate in conversation. AITA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to tell my SIL (sister-in-law) to shut up during dinner. Let me start by understanding the situation better. My SIL is someone who is really proud of not watching TV, not listening to pop music, and not having Facebook. She often interrupts conversations to mention these things, and she does it in a way that's more about her superiority than just stating her preferences. A few days ago, during dinner, my 14-year-old sister started talking about a Marvel movie she watched and was looking forward to the sequel. My SIL interrupted and said she had never watched any Marvel movies and that they seemed pretty awful. I got really upset because I don't understand why my SIL feels the need to be so rude and dismissive, especially towards a teenager. So, I told her to shut up, adding that not everything has to be about her and what she likes. She blushed and didn't say anything more, and my brother didn't say anything either. But later, he messaged me saying that this was my way of always hating his wife and that I'm a bad person who doesn't want her to participate in conversations. Now, I'm wondering if I did the right thing or not. On one hand, I felt justified because my SIL was being rude and dismissive, especially towards my younger sister. On the other hand, telling someone to shut up is pretty harsh, and it might have made things worse between me and my brother, especially since he took it personally. I also need to consider the dynamics of the family. My brother is married to my SIL, so he might be more defensive of her, which could explain why he took my action so negatively. Maybe I should have handled the situation differently, like addressing her behavior in a more constructive way instead of just telling her to shut up. Another thing to think about is the impact on my sister. She was talking about something she enjoyed, and my SIL's comment could have made her feel bad or uninterested in sharing her thoughts in the future. By standing up for her, I was trying to protect her feelings, but my approach might have been too aggressive. I also wonder about the broader implications of this incident. If I continue to react this way in family gatherings, it could lead to more tension and conflict. It might be better to find a way to communicate my feelings without being confrontational. In summary, while I felt that my SIL's behavior was inappropriate and deserved a response, telling her to shut up might not have been the best approach. It led to hurt feelings and tension with my brother, and it might have negatively impacted my sister's willingness to participate in conversations. Maybe there's a more diplomatic way to address such situations in the future.
